intro: One cat is nice. A basket of kittens is even better! In this unit you will learn to talk about more than one thing in Spanish. Gato becomes gatos. Flor becomes flores.
You will also learn to tell what things are like. Is the dog big or little? Is the girl happy or sad? You will say el perro grande and la niña feliz, and make the words match.
bigQuestion: How do Spanish words change to show how many and what things are like?

timeline.t: Add -s to words that end in a vowel: gato, gatos.
Add -es to words that end in a consonant: flor, flores.
Change z to c before -es: lápiz, lápices.
Change el to los and la to las.
Name big, little, tall, short, happy and sad.
Put the describing word after the thing: el perro grande.
Make words match: la gata pequeña, los perros grandes.

words.d: the cats — add -s after a vowel
the flowers — add -es after a consonant
the pencils — z changes to c, then -es
big — the same for el and la words
little — pequeña for la words
tall — the opposite of bajo
happy — plural is felices
sad — the opposite of feliz

test.q: What is the plural of el libro?
test.why: Both words change: el becomes los and libro gets -s.

test.q: What is the plural of la flor?
test.why: Flor ends in a consonant, so add -es, and la becomes las.

test.q: What is the plural of el pez?
test.why: Z changes to c, then add -es: los peces.

test.q: How do you say two cats?
test.why: After dos there is more than one, so add -s: dos gatos.

test.q: How do you say the big house?
test.why: The describing word goes after the thing, and casa goes with la: la casa grande.
Niña goes with la, so alto changes to alta.

test.q: What is the opposite of grande?
test.why: Grande means big and pequeño means little.

test.q: What is the plural of el gato feliz?
test.why: Everything is plural, and feliz changes z to c before -es.

test.q: Which word means the for many la words?
test.why: La becomes las for more than one: las casas.

write.prompt: Draw some animals. Label them or say 3 sentences in Spanish, like: Tres perros grandes. Una gata pequeña. Los gatos felices. Use a number, the thing, and a describing word that matches.
tips: Put the describing word after the thing.
Add -s or -es when there is more than one.
Check el, la, los and las.

title: One and Many, Big and Little

chapters.title: More Than One
chapters.bigQuestion: How do Spanish words change when there is more than one?

story.title: A Basket of Kittens
story.kicker: One cat at Tomás's house turns into a whole basket of kittens.
paragraphs: Tomás has one cat. Her name is Luna. "Tengo un gato," he says. That means "I have a cat." Luna is soft and gray. She sleeps in a basket by the door.
One morning Tomás looks in the basket. He sees Luna. He sees something else too. There are tiny kittens! "¡Mamá, mira!" he shouts. That means "Mom, look!"
Tomás counts them. Uno, dos, tres, cuatro. "¡Cuatro gatitos!" he says. That means four kittens. The word gatito got an s at the end. Now it means more than one.
Mamá smiles. "Un gato," she says, pointing to Luna. "Los gatitos," she says, pointing to the babies. Tomás hears it. One word becomes many words with a little s.
story.think: What do you have more than one of at home? How would you say it in Spanish?

lessons.title: One Cat, Two Cats
lessons.mainIdea: When a word ends in a vowel, add -s to mean more than one.
reading: Look at one cat. In Spanish it is *gato* (cat). Now look at two cats. They are *gatos* (cats). We just added an s.
Gato ends in o. The letters a, e, i, o, u are vowels. When a word ends in a vowel, add -s. Casa becomes casas. Mesa becomes mesas.
More than one is called plural. English does this too: cat, cats. So this one is easy for you!

words.d: the cat — one cat
the cats — more than one cat

look.title: Add the S
look.text: Look at the pictures in your mind. One ball: la pelota. Many balls: las pelotas. One house: la casa. Many houses: las casas. One book: el libro. Many books: los libros.
look.prompt: One apple is la manzana. How do you say many apples?

check.q: What does gatos mean?
check.why: Gato means cat. Adding -s makes it plural: gatos means cats.

check.q: Casa ends in a vowel. What is the plural?
check.why: Casa ends in the vowel a, so we just add -s: casas.

check.q: Which word means more than one book?
check.why: Libro ends in o, a vowel, so add -s: libros.

lessons.title: Counting Plural Things
lessons.mainIdea: After a number bigger than one, the thing is plural: tres perros.
reading: Picture one dog. That is *un perro* (a dog). Now picture three dogs. That is *tres perros* (three dogs).
After dos, tres, cuatro or any bigger number, the word gets an s. Dos gatos. Cinco libros. Diez casas.
Uno is different. With just one, there is no s. Un perro. Una casa. Only one, so no plural.

words.d: the dog — one dog
three dogs — the s shows more than one

look.title: How Many Dogs?
look.prompt: Which row has no s at the end of perro? Why?

check.q: How do you say five dogs?
check.why: After cinco there is more than one, and perro ends in a vowel, so add -s: cinco perros.

check.q: Which one is right for one dog?
check.why: With just one, there is no plural s: un perro.

check.q: What does dos gatos mean?
check.why: Dos means two and gatos means cats.

lessons.title: One Flower, Many Flowers
lessons.mainIdea: When a word ends in a consonant, add -es: flor becomes flores.
reading: Look at one flower. It is *la flor* (the flower). Flor ends in r. R is not a vowel. It is a consonant.
When a word ends in a consonant, add -es. Flor becomes *flores* (flowers). Tren becomes trenes. Color becomes colores.
Why -es? Try to say flors. It is hard to say! The e makes it easy. Say it slowly: flo-res.

words.d: the flower — ends in r
the flowers — add -es after a consonant

look.title: A Garden
look.text: Picture a garden. There is one big tree and many flowers: las flores. A train goes by: el tren. Then more trains: los trenes. The flowers have many colors: los colores.
look.prompt: Say the plural of el tren and la flor out loud.

check.q: What is the plural of flor?
check.why: Flor ends in the consonant r, so add -es: flores.

check.q: What is the plural of tren?
check.why: Tren ends in the consonant n, so add -es: trenes.

check.q: Which word needs -es to be plural?
check.why: Color ends in r, a consonant, so it becomes colores. Gato and casa end in vowels.

lessons.title: Z Changes to C
lessons.mainIdea: When a word ends in z, change z to c and add -es: lápiz becomes lápices.
reading: Look at one pencil. It is *el lápiz* (the pencil). It ends in z. Now look at many pencils.
The z changes to c. Then add -es. Lápiz becomes *lápices* (pencils). Pez (fish) becomes peces. Luz (light) becomes luces.
Many kids write lápizes. That is a mistake. Remember: the z turns into c, then add -es.

words.d: the pencil — ends in z
the pencils — z changes to c, then add -es
the fish (a live fish) — plural is peces

look.title: Z to C
look.text: Watch the change. lápiz: take off z, put on c, add es. lápices. pez: take off z, put on c, add es. peces. luz: take off z, put on c, add es. luces.
look.prompt: Try it yourself: what is the plural of luz?

check.q: What is the plural of lápiz?
check.why: Z changes to c, then add -es: lápices.

check.q: What does peces mean?
check.why: Pez means fish. Peces is the plural, more than one fish.

check.q: What happens to the z in luz?
check.why: In the plural, z changes to c: luz becomes luces.

lessons.title: El Becomes Los
lessons.mainIdea: El means the for one thing. Los means the for more than one.
reading: Look at one cat. It is *el* gato. Now look at many cats. It is *los* gatos. The word the changed!
El goes with one thing. Los goes with many things. El libro, los libros. El perro, los perros.
In English, the never changes. In Spanish it does. So two words change: el becomes los, and gato becomes gatos.

words.d: the — for one thing like el perro
the — for many things like los perros

look.title: Two Words, Two Changes
look.text: el gato → los gatos. el libro → los libros. el lápiz → los lápices. el tren → los trenes. Look at each pair. The first word changes. The last word changes too.
look.prompt: Say the plural of el perro. Did you change both words?

check.q: What is the plural of el libro?
check.why: Both words change: el becomes los and libro becomes libros.

check.q: Which word means the for many things like gatos?
check.why: Los goes with many things like gatos: los gatos.

check.q: What is wrong with el perros?
check.why: Perros is plural, so the must be plural too: los perros.

lessons.title: La Becomes Las
lessons.mainIdea: La means the for one thing. Las means the for more than one.
reading: Look at one house. It is *la* casa (the house). Now look at many houses. It is *las* casas.
La goes with one thing. *Las* goes with many things. La flor, las flores. La mesa, las mesas.
Just add s to la! La becomes las. Casa becomes casas. Both words get an s at the end.

words.d: the — for one thing like la casa
the — for many things like las casas

look.title: Setting the Table
look.text: Abuela sets the table. "La mesa," she says. She puts out plates: los platos. She puts out cups: las tazas. She puts flowers in the middle: las flores. "¡Listo!" she says. That means ready!
look.prompt: Which words in the story go with las?

check.q: What is the plural of la flor?
check.why: La becomes las, and flor becomes flores: las flores.

check.q: What is the plural of la mesa?
check.why: La becomes las, and mesa gets -s: las mesas.

check.q: Las casas means…
check.why: Las and casas are both plural, so it means the houses.

review.q: What is the plural of el gato?
review.why: Both words change: el becomes los and gato becomes gatos.

review.q: What is the plural of la flor?
review.why: Flor ends in a consonant, so add -es. La becomes las: las flores.

review.q: What is the plural of el lápiz?
review.why: Z changes to c, then add -es. El becomes los: los lápices.

review.q: How do you say four houses?
review.why: Casa ends in a vowel, so add -s: cuatro casas.

review.q: In the story, what does cuatro gatitos mean?
review.why: Cuatro means four and gatitos means kittens.

review.q: Which word ends in a vowel and just needs -s?
review.why: Libro ends in the vowel o, so it becomes libros.

chapters.title: Big, Little, Happy, Sad
chapters.bigQuestion: How do we tell what something is like in Spanish?

story.title: The Elephant and the Mouse
story.kicker: A big elephant and a little mouse find out they can be friends.
paragraphs: In a green park lives an elephant. He is very big. In Spanish we say el elefante grande. That means the big elephant. He is also sad. He has no friends.
Under a rock lives a mouse. She is very little. In Spanish we say la ratona pequeña. That means the little mouse. She is sad too. She is all alone.
One day the mouse sees the elephant. "¡Hola!" she says. The elephant looks down. "¡Hola!" he says. They play all day in the park.
Now the big elephant is feliz. That means happy. The little mouse is feliz too. Big or little, happy or sad, they are good friends now.
story.think: Who is big and who is little in the story? How did they feel at the end?

lessons.title: Grande and Pequeño
lessons.mainIdea: Grande means big. Pequeño means little.
reading: Picture an elephant. It is very big. In Spanish, big is *grande* (big). El elefante grande.
Now picture a mouse. It is very little. Little is *pequeño* (little). El ratón pequeño.
Grande and pequeño are opposites. Opposites mean very different things, like big and little.

words.d: big — el elefante grande, the big elephant
little or small — el ratón pequeño, the little mouse

look.title: Big or Little?
look.text: Look at the playground. There is a big slide and a little ball. There is a big tree and a little bird. The tree is grande. The bird is pequeño.
look.prompt: Name one thing in your room that is grande and one that is pequeño.

check.q: What does grande mean?
check.why: Grande means big.

check.q: Which word is the opposite of grande?
check.why: Pequeño means little, the opposite of big.

check.q: An elephant is…
check.why: An elephant is very big, so it is grande.

lessons.title: Alto and Bajo
lessons.mainIdea: Alto means tall. Bajo means short.
reading: Picture a giraffe. It is very tall. In Spanish, tall is *alto* (tall). La jirafa is tall.
Now picture a little puppy. It is short. Short is *bajo* (short). Alto and bajo are opposites.
Be careful! Bajo means short, like not tall. It does not mean a short time or a short trip.

words.d: tall — el árbol alto, the tall tree
short (not tall) — el perro bajo, the short dog

look.title: Tall and Short
look.text: Papá stands next to his son Diego. Papá is tall: alto. Diego is short: bajo. Then Diego stands on a chair. "¡Ahora soy alto!" he says. That means "Now I am tall!"
look.prompt: Who in your family is alto? Who is bajo?

check.q: What does alto mean?
check.why: Alto means tall.

check.q: Which word is the opposite of alto?
check.why: Bajo means short, the opposite of tall.

check.q: A very tall tree is el árbol…
check.why: Alto means tall: el árbol alto.

lessons.title: Feliz and Triste
lessons.mainIdea: Feliz means happy. Triste means sad.
reading: Picture a kid at a birthday party. She smiles and laughs. She is *feliz* (happy).
Now picture a kid who lost his ball. He frowns. He is *triste* (sad). Feliz and triste are opposites.
Feliz and triste stay the same for a boy or a girl. El niño feliz. La niña feliz.

words.d: happy — like a smile at a party
sad — like a frown when you lose something

look.title: Faces
look.text: Draw two faces in the air with your finger. The first face has a big smile. It is feliz. The second face has a frown and a tear. It is triste.
look.prompt: Make a feliz face. Now make a triste face. Say each word.

check.q: What does triste mean?
check.why: Triste means sad.

check.q: A kid smiles at a party. The kid is…
check.why: A smiling kid is happy: feliz.

check.q: Which word is the opposite of feliz?
check.why: Triste means sad, the opposite of happy.

lessons.title: The Describing Word Goes After
lessons.mainIdea: In Spanish, the describing word comes after the thing: el perro grande.
reading: In English we say the big dog. Big comes first. In Spanish we say *el perro grande*. Grande comes after!
The thing comes first. Then the describing word. La casa pequeña. El niño feliz. El árbol alto.
English speakers often say el grande perro. That sounds wrong. Say the thing first, then what it is like.

words.d: the big dog — the describing word grande comes after perro

look.title: Thing First
look.text: English: the happy cat. Spanish: el gato feliz. English: the tall tree. Spanish: el árbol alto. English: the sad dog. Spanish: el perro triste. The thing comes first every time.
look.prompt: How do you say the happy dog in Spanish?

check.q: How do you say the big dog?
check.why: In Spanish the describing word goes after the thing: el perro grande.

check.q: What does el gato feliz mean?
check.why: Gato is cat and feliz is happy: the happy cat.

check.q: Which one has the right Spanish order?
check.why: The thing comes first, then the describing word: el árbol alto.

lessons.title: Matching -o and -a
lessons.mainIdea: Describing words ending in -o change to -a to match la words.
reading: Look at a little boy cat. He is el gato *pequeño*. Now look at a little girl cat. She is la gata *pequeña*.
Pequeño ends in o. With la gata it changes to a. The words match. Alto becomes alta. Bajo becomes baja.
Grande, feliz and triste do not end in o. They stay the same. El gato grande. La gata grande.

words.d: little — goes with el words: el gato pequeño
little — goes with la words: la gata pequeña

look.title: Make It Match
look.text: el niño alto, la niña alta. el perro bajo, la casa baja. el gato pequeño, la mesa pequeña. el perro grande, la casa grande. Grande does not change.
look.prompt: How do you say the tall girl? Remember to match the -a.

check.q: How do you say the little house?
check.why: Casa goes with la, so pequeño changes to pequeña, and it goes after: la casa pequeña.

check.q: Which one is right?
check.why: Niña goes with la, so alto changes to alta.

check.q: Which describing word stays the same for el and la?
check.why: Grande does not end in o, so it stays the same: el perro grande, la casa grande.

lessons.title: Many Big Dogs
lessons.mainIdea: When the thing is plural, the describing word gets -s or -es too.
reading: Look at one big dog: el perro grande. Now look at many big dogs: *los perros grandes*. Every word gets an s!
Pequeña becomes pequeñas: las casas pequeñas. Triste becomes tristes: los niños tristes.
Feliz ends in z. Remember the rule? Z changes to c, then add -es. Feliz becomes felices: los gatos felices.

words.d: the big dogs — every word is plural
happy (for many) — feliz changes z to c and adds -es

look.title: Everything Gets an S
look.text: One: el gato pequeño. Many: los gatos pequeños. One: la niña alta. Many: las niñas altas. One: el niño feliz. Many: los niños felices. Count the s sounds!
look.prompt: Say the plural of la casa grande.

check.q: What is the plural of el perro grande?
check.why: Every word becomes plural: los perros grandes.

check.q: What is the plural of feliz?
check.why: Z changes to c, then add -es: felices.

check.q: Which one means the little houses?
check.why: Casas goes with las and -a, and everything is plural: las casas pequeñas.

review.q: How do you say the sad dog?
review.why: The describing word goes after the thing: el perro triste.
Gata goes with la, so pequeño becomes pequeña.

review.q: In the story, how is the elephant at the end?
review.why: At the end the elephant has a friend, so he is feliz, happy.

review.q: What is the opposite of alto?
review.why: Alto means tall and bajo means short.

review.q: What is the plural of el niño feliz?
review.why: Everything is plural, and feliz changes z to c before -es: los niños felices.
